_doc: Templates grammaticaux pour générer la trace écrite et les fiches PDF. Chaque entrée contient un libellé, 3 exemples canoniques (affirmative/négative/interrogative), et une remarque pédagogique. La fonction matchTemplate(langue) sélectionne le bon template par mots-clés.

to-be.label: Le verbe TO BE au présent

examples.affirmative: I am French.
examples.negative: She is not tired.

to-be.remark: Formes contractées : I'm, you're, he's, she's, it's, we're, they're.

have-got.label: HAVE GOT — possession

examples.affirmative: I have got a brother.
examples.negative: She has not got a sister.

have-got.remark: S'utilise surtout en anglais britannique pour exprimer la possession.

present-simple.label: Le présent simple

examples.affirmative: I play football every day.
examples.negative: She does not play tennis.

present-simple.remark: On utilise le présent simple pour parler d'habitudes, de vérités générales et de goûts.

present-continuous.label: Le présent en BE + V-ing

examples.affirmative: I am playing football right now.
examples.negative: She is not watching TV.

present-continuous.remark: On utilise le présent continu pour une action en train de se dérouler au moment où l'on parle (now, at the moment).

present-perfect.label: Le present perfect (have/has + V-en)

examples.affirmative: I have lived here for five years.
examples.negative: She has not seen the film yet.

present-perfect.remark: Action commencée dans le passé qui continue au présent (since/for) ou expérience passée non datée (ever, never, already, yet).

past-simple.label: Le prétérit simple

examples.affirmative: Yesterday, I visited the museum.
examples.negative: She did not go to school last Monday.

past-simple.remark: On utilise le prétérit pour les actions terminées datées (yesterday, last week, in 2020, ago).

past-continuous.label: Le past continuous (was/were + V-ing)

examples.affirmative: She was reading when I called.
examples.negative: We were not watching the news.

past-continuous.remark: Décrit une action en cours dans le passé, souvent interrompue par une autre (au prétérit).

past-perfect.label: Le past perfect (had + V-en)

examples.affirmative: By 2020, she had finished her studies.
examples.negative: He had not arrived when the meeting started.

past-perfect.remark: Exprime une action antérieure à un autre moment du passé. Très utile en récit (storytelling).

future-will.label: Le futur en WILL

examples.affirmative: Tomorrow, I will go to the beach.
examples.negative: She will not come tonight.

future-will.remark: On utilise will pour des prédictions, promesses, décisions spontanées ou faits futurs.

future-going-to.label: Le futur proche en BE GOING TO

examples.affirmative: I am going to visit my grandmother next weekend.
examples.negative: She is not going to travel this summer.

future-going-to.remark: Exprime une intention ou un projet déjà décidé.

modals.label: Les modaux : can / could / must / should

examples.affirmative: I can swim very well.
examples.negative: She cannot drive yet.

modals.remark: Les modaux expriment la capacité (can), la possibilité (may, might), l'obligation (must), le conseil (should). Toujours suivis de la base verbale.

comparatives.label: Les comparatifs

examples.affirmative: Madagascar is bigger than Iceland.
examples.negative: This book is not as interesting as the other one.
examples.interrogative: Is the Nile longer than the Amazon?

comparatives.remark: Adj. court : -er than. Adj. long : more … than. Égalité : as … as. Comparatifs irréguliers : good/better, bad/worse, far/further.

superlatives.label: Les superlatifs

examples.affirmative: Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
examples.negative: This is not the most exciting book I've read.
examples.interrogative: Who is the best player on the team?

superlatives.remark: Adj. court : the -est. Adj. long : the most …. Toujours précédé de the.

passive.label: La voix passive

examples.affirmative: This museum was built in 1850.
examples.negative: The book was not written by Hemingway.

passive.remark: Structure : sujet + be (au temps voulu) + participe passé. L'agent peut être introduit par by.

conditional.label: Le conditionnel (would + base verbale)

examples.affirmative: If I had time, I would travel the world.
examples.negative: She would not go there alone.

conditional.remark: Structures conditionnelles : type 1 (réel : if + present, will), type 2 (irréel : if + preterit, would), type 3 (passé irréel : if + past perfect, would have).

there-is.label: THERE IS / THERE ARE

examples.affirmative: There is a beautiful market in Analakely.
examples.negative: There are not any clouds in the sky.

there-is.remark: There is + nom singulier ou indénombrable. There are + nom pluriel.

questions-wh.label: Les mots interrogatifs (Wh- words)

examples.affirmative: What is your name?
examples.negative: Where do you live?

questions-wh.remark: What (quoi), Who (qui), Where (où), When (quand), Why (pourquoi), How (comment), Which (lequel), Whose (à qui).

relative-clauses.label: Les subordonnées relatives

examples.affirmative: The book which / that I'm reading is fascinating.
examples.negative: She is the only person who doesn't agree.
examples.interrogative: Is this the woman whose daughter won the prize?

relative-clauses.remark: Who (personnes), which (choses), that (les deux, défini), whose (possession), where (lieu), when (temps). On peut omettre le pronom relatif quand il est COD.

reported-speech.label: Le discours rapporté

examples.affirmative: She said (that) she was tired.
examples.negative: He told me (that) he did not know the answer.
examples.interrogative: She asked me if I had seen the film.

reported-speech.remark: Recul des temps : présent → prétérit, prétérit → past perfect, will → would. Modifications des marqueurs temporels (now → then, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day).

mixed-conditionals.label: Les conditionnels mixtes

examples.affirmative: If I had studied harder (passé), I would be a doctor now (présent).
examples.negative: If she were not so shy, she would have spoken at the meeting.
examples.interrogative: What would you do now if you had won the lottery?

mixed-conditionals.remark: Mélange entre conditionnel type 2 (présent irréel) et type 3 (passé irréel) : exprime une conséquence présente d'une condition passée — ou l'inverse. Très utile pour analyser des choix historiques.

modals-probability.label: Les modaux de probabilité et de jugement

examples.affirmative: She must have left early (forte probabilité passée).
examples.negative: He cannot be at home — his car isn't here.

modals-probability.remark: Probabilité présente : must / may / might / can't + base. Probabilité passée : must / may / might / can't have + V-en. Échelle de certitude : must (sûr) > may > might > could > can't (sûr que non).

emphatic-structures.label: Les structures emphatiques

examples.affirmative: It is diversity that makes our society strong.
examples.negative: What I really value is open dialogue, not silence.
examples.interrogative: Never have I seen such a powerful speech.

emphatic-structures.remark: Cleft sentences (it is … that, what … is) et inversion après adverbes négatifs (never, rarely, not only) servent à mettre en relief une information.

gerund-infinitive.label: Gérondif et infinitif (V-ing / to + base)

examples.affirmative: I enjoy reading novels but I want to write one.
examples.negative: She decided not to go; he avoided telling the truth.
examples.interrogative: Do you prefer watching films or going to the theatre?

gerund-infinitive.remark: Verbes + V-ing : enjoy, avoid, mind, finish, suggest. Verbes + to + base : want, decide, hope, refuse, agree. Quelques verbes acceptent les deux avec un sens différent (remember, forget, stop).

phrasal-verbs.label: Les phrasal verbs

examples.affirmative: She looked up the word in the dictionary.
examples.negative: He did not give up despite the difficulties.

phrasal-verbs.remark: Verbe + particule (preposition / adverbe) qui modifie le sens : look up (chercher), look after (s'occuper de), give up (abandonner), find out (découvrir). Souvent indissociables du sens littéral.

_default.label: Faits de langue de la séquence

examples.affirmative: Madagascar is an island in the Indian Ocean.
examples.negative: Most students do not have the same opportunities.

_default.remark: Ces exemples illustrent la mobilisation de la structure de la séquence en contexte. La fiche d'activité PDF contient les tableaux de conjugaison et les exercices d'application détaillés.
